objective: Tree-level e+e- -> mu+mu- via one photon: differential and integrated cross section

model.description: e+e- -> mu+mu- through one s-channel photon, lowest order

assumptions: one s-channel photon, tree level (order alpha^2 in the cross section)
massless electrons, muon mass m kept
unpolarized beams: average over the 4 initial spin states, sum over final spins
point-like fermions, no Z exchange, no radiative corrections

conventions.unit_system: natural-HEP: GeV for energies, s in GeV^2; cross sections quoted in pb (1 nb = 1000 pb)
conventions.renormalization_scheme: not-applicable at tree level; alpha is a fixed input (its value enters only through the reference constant below)
conventions.scales: not-applicable at tree level with fixed alpha: no renormalization or factorization scale enters and alpha is not run to sqrt(s), so there is no scale variation or scale uncertainty
conventions.angle_definition: theta between the incoming e- and the outgoing mu- in the c.m. frame
conventions.spin_treatment: unpolarized beams: average over the four initial spin states, sum over final spins
conventions.mass_approximation: electrons massless; muon mass kept in the derivation, massless (beta -> 1) in the numerical prediction
conventions.qedbench:reference_constant: 4 pi alpha^2 / 3 converted to nb GeV^2 is taken as 86.8 nb GeV^2 from PDG eq. (51.3) [qedbench:C02], three significant figures

extension.order: tree level, O(alpha^2) in the cross section

parameters.muon_mass: symbolic m in the derivation; 0 in the numerical prediction

validity_domain.sqrt_s: well above 2 m_mu and well below m_Z [Proposal: benchmark point 10 GeV]

checks_not_run: independent value of 4 pi alpha^2 / 3 in nb GeV^2 from separately read alpha and (hbar c)^2
quantitative Z-exchange and gamma-Z interference size at the benchmark point
QED radiative corrections and running of alpha
numerical muon-mass correction (no cited muon mass)
formal proof (SymPy steps trusted, not verified)

references_read.citation: Cross-Section Formulae for Specific Processes (Review of Particle Physics, section 51); H. Baer and R.N. Cahn (revised August 2019); in F. Takahashi et al. (Particle Data Group), Int. J. Mod. Phys. A 41, 2630011 (2026)
